title: Directed unions of pointed refinements preserving two classes
statement: Fix a diagram X:J→Cᵒᵖ with J nonempty directed, a presheaf P and two classes s,s′ in colim(X⋙P). In the category of strict diagram refinements [def-trf-point-system-diagram], take the under-category of X. Call an extension good when its index is nonempty directed and the canonical images of s,s′ [def-trf-point-system-refinement-map] are distinct. For any nonempty directed partial order A in Type w, a colimit cocone of A-indexed good extensions has good apex. Consequently the full category of good extensions has colimits of every such shape.

source.place: Tag 00YP, proof of lemma-refine-all-at-once; strict refinements preceding Tag 00YO

proof.text: Forget the under-category cocone to index posets. The under forgetful functor preserves connected colimits, the diagram-index functor preserves filtered colimits, and PartOrdEmb→Type preserves them. Hence every index in the apex comes from a stage.

source.place: Tag 00YP, proof of lemma-refine-all-at-once; strict refinements preceding Tag 00YO

proof.text: The ranges of the stage embeddings form increasing directed subsets of the apex, cover it, and contain the original indices by the under-category triangle. They are a chain presentation. Each stage is order-isomorphic to its range; the inverse parametrization identifies the range diagram with the old diagram, and maps on colimits compose. Equality of original images in a range stage would therefore contradict goodness of the old stage. Apply separation in a chain union.

source.place: Tag 00YP, proof of lemma-refine-all-at-once; strict refinements preceding Tag 00YO

proof.text: The colimit apex is good by the preceding steps. Lift its cocone and its universal maps to the full subcategory of good objects; fullness and faithfulness give the colimit universal property there.
